# Initial CI qualification repairs

The first PR #462 CI run on `cfa05282` exposed two qualification issues. No production numerical implementation or tolerance changed to correct them.

- `TestPortableDensityEventEvaluation` measured persistent storage before the first full-grid scalar derivative prepared the compact kernel's scalar resources. The probe now explicitly prepares its constant kernel and borrows it for field evaluation. Both retained-storage measurements include the borrowed kernel's full capacity. Scientific comparisons, first-event counters and caller-coefficient checks remain unchanged. Replay additionally checks that retained storage stays fixed and no density/event workspace remains live. No density warmup hides recovery or computation counts.
- `repositoryTracksOnlySourceProducts` correctly rejected a `.tar.gz` evidence container under its existing native-product suffix rule. The archive contained only text, but its format violated the repository convention. Its 17 members were converted to the existing compressed JSON text-metadata format, preserving every member hash and original raw hash. The repository test was not weakened. The converted receipt records the original container hash as history.

`hosted-failures.json.gz` retains the original Release density, source-product and sanitizer-backed density failures from [the initial run](https://github.com/JeffreyEarly/wave-vortex-model/actions/runs/34454835992), with exact text hashes. The fresh local receipt and bundle record the corrected probe source, Release/sanitizer binaries, source invariance and focused MATLAB test results. Only failed methods were rerun; previously successful numerical/build and performance campaigns were not repeated for these probe/container corrections. Required hosted CI runs again on the repaired commit.

Focused repair qualification passes: all three density methods with Release reference/native (44 cases), all three with ASan/UBSan reference (22 cases), and the tracked-source-products method. macOS LeakSanitizer is unsupported and unclaimed; ASan/UBSan remain active. Source and probe binary hashes stayed unchanged during the successful runs.
